question: According to Table 6B-3, what taper lengths are used for shifting, shoulder, and one-lane two-way traffic tapers?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Per Table 6B-3, a shifting taper should be at least 0.5 L, a shoulder taper at least 0.33 L, and a one-lane, two-way traffic taper should be 50 feet minimum and 100 feet maximum. These values are echoed in the Guidance provisions of Section 6B.08, with L calculated using the formulas in Table 6B-4. Guidance (recommended): - "A shifting taper should have a length of approximately ½ L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4)." - "If used, shoulder tapers should have a length of approximately ¹⁄3 L (see Tables 6B-3 and 6B-4). If a shoulder is used as a travel lane, either through practice or during a TTC activity, a normal merging or shifting taper should be used." - For the one-lane, two-way section: "A taper having a minimum length of 50 feet and a maximum length of 100 feet with channelizing devices at approximately 20-foot spacing should be used to guide traffic into the one-lane section, and a downstream taper should be used to guide traffic back into their original lane." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 6B-3 lists taper lengths of "at least 0.5 L" for a Shifting Taper, "at least 0.33 L" for a Shoulder Taper, and "50 feet minimum, 100 feet maximum" for a One-Lane, Two-Way Traffic Taper, with a note to use Table 6B-4 to calculate L. [Image 2] Figure 6B-2 (Types of Tapers and Buffer Spaces) graphically depicts shifting tapers dimensioned as 1/2 L and a shoulder taper dimensioned as 1/3 L. [Image 3] Page 776 shows Section 6B.08 Guidance provisions specifying the ½ L shifting taper, ⅓ L shoulder taper, and the 50–100 foot one-lane, two-way taper. [Image 4] Page 775 shows Table 6B-3 (Taper Length Criteria for Temporary Traffic Control Zones) alongside Table 6B-4 (Formulas for Determining Taper Length: L = WS²/60 for 40 mph or less; L = WS for 45 mph or more). [Image 5] Figure 6P-39 (Median Crossover on a Freeway, TA-39) shows an application of shoulder tapers and 1/2 L shifting taper dimensions in a temporary traffic control layout. Citations: - Table 6B-3 (p.775) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §8 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §10 (p.776) - Section 6B.08 Guidance §14 (p.776) - Page 815 - Page 816 - Page 817 - Page 978
gold_answer: A shifting taper is at least 0.5L, a shoulder taper is at least 0.33L, and a one-lane two-way traffic taper is 50 feet minimum and 100 feet maximum.
